title: Comparison 5 · Repeated rotations — accumulated interpolation error
summary: One 30° rotation vs ten 3° rotations via a DO + flow.state feedback loop. Each extra spline interpolation blurs the result slightly; the diff image shows how fast that stacks up.

steps.title: Measure cumulative interpolation loss with a DO loop
steps.body:
Each spline interpolation acts like a tiny low-pass filter, so **for the same total 30°**:

  • **One 30° rotation**: one interpolation's worth of loss.
  • **10° × 3 rotations**: three interpolations' worth (cumulative).

Gives different results.

Tutorial layout:

  1. **Circular mask** confines the image inside radius 120 and zeroes the outside. The disk's support is rotation-invariant, so **content stays within the box at every angle** — no side effects from corner clipping.
  2. **DO loop + `flow.state`** sets up a feedback: 'this iteration's output becomes the next iteration's input.'
  3. Subtract the single-30° result from the DO version with arith.binop — the diff image shows **pure cumulative interpolation loss**.

`flow.state` is a special node that carries a value across iterations: `initial` is the starting value from outside the loop; `value_in` is the value you feed in at the end of this iteration (becomes next iteration's state); `value_out` is the current value visible at the start of this iteration.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Checkerboard** (256×256).

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.checker` shows its image before we start masking.

steps.title: Drop the Circular mask node
steps.body: From Masking, drag **Circular mask** (`mask.circle`). Confines the image inside a circle and zeroes the outside so corner clipping during rotation doesn't eat information.

steps.title: Wire Checker → Mask
steps.body: Drag Checker's `image` output to Circular mask's `image` input.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. `mask.circle`'s default behaviour becomes a baseline before we tune the radius and background.

steps.title: Click Mask
steps.body: Click Circular mask. Set `outer_radius` (the radius to keep) and `background_mode` / `background` (value outside).

steps.title: Set outer_radius to 120
steps.body: Enter **120** in `outer_radius`. Content inside radius 120 is preserved (image is 256×256). A circular support is rotation-invariant, so no information bleeds into the corners at any angle (128 → 120 leaves a small safety margin).

steps.title: Set background_mode to external
steps.body: Change `background_mode` to **`external`**. Outside the circle becomes `background` (scalar, default **0**). The default `average` (≈ 0.5) would make a grey rim; 0 gives a clean black outside.

steps.title: Pipeline X · drop Rotate
steps.body: From Geometry, drag **Rotate** (`geom.rotate`). This is X (one-shot 30° rotation). Place it outside the DO loop.

steps.title: Wire Mask → Rotate (X)
steps.body: Drag Mask's `image` output to Rotate (X)'s `image` input. The masked disk is the input.

steps.title: Click Rotate (X)
steps.body: Click this Rotate.

steps.title: Set angle_deg to 30
steps.body: Enter **30** in `angle_deg`. X: a single-interpolation 30° rotation.

steps.title: Drop the DO loop
steps.body: From Control, drag **DO loop** (`flow.do`). We'll place Rotate and flow.state inside it to accumulate 3 passes of rotation.

steps.title: Drop flow.state inside DO
steps.body: From Control, drag **Loop state** (`flow.state`) and drop it **inside the DO container frame**. This node holds the 'current iteration's image'.

steps.title: Drop Rotate inside DO
steps.body: From Geometry, drag **Rotate** and drop it **inside the DO container**. This is Y — it applies 10° per iteration.

steps.title: Wire Mask → state.initial
steps.body: Drag from Mask (outside the DO) to `flow.state`'s **`initial`** input inside (top handle). This is the value state sees on iteration 1 = the masked checkerboard.

steps.title: Wire state.value_out → Rotate (Y)
steps.body: Drag from `flow.state`'s `value_out` output to Rotate (Y)'s `image` input inside the DO. At the start of every iteration, the current state value flows into Rotate.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. `geom.rotate`'s default behaviour inside the loop becomes a baseline before we wire the feedback.

steps.title: Wire Rotate (Y) → state.value_in (feedback)
steps.body: Drag from Rotate (Y)'s `image` output to `flow.state`'s **`value_in`** input (bottom handle). This stores Rotate's result as the next iteration's state value — rotations now accumulate.

steps.title: Click Rotate (Y)
steps.body: Click the Rotate inside the DO.

steps.title: Set angle_deg to 10
steps.body: Enter **10** in `angle_deg`. 10° per iteration, 3 iterations → 30° total — matches X.

steps.title: Click the DO loop
steps.body: Click the DO container header to select it. `start` / `end` / `step` appear in the Inspector.

steps.title: Set end to 3
steps.body: Change `end` to **3**. With default `start=1, step=1` and `end=3` we get 3 iterations (i = 1, 2, 3).

steps.title: Drop arith.binop for the X − Y diff
steps.body: From Arithmetic, drag **Arithmetic · a ∘ b**. Place it outside the DO. We'll compare X's output against the DO's final Rotate (Y) output.

steps.title: Wire Rotate (X) → binop.a
steps.body: Drag from the outside Rotate (X)'s `image` output to arith.binop's `a` input.

steps.title: Wire Rotate (Y) → binop.b
steps.body: Drag from the DO-internal Rotate (Y)'s `image` output to arith.binop's `b` input. Wires can cross the DO boundary — the value from the final iteration is read.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. `arith.binop`'s default behaviour becomes a baseline before we flip the op to sub.

steps.title: Click binop
steps.body: Click arith.binop.

steps.title: Set op to sub
steps.body: Change `op` to **`sub`** — output is `X − Y`.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body:
Press ▶ Run graph. Mask → fork → X and DO (Y) → diff all execute. What to notice:

  1. **Compare X and Y previews** — both are the masked disk rotated by a total of 30°. Outside the circle stays 0 (black). Y should look **slightly more blurred** (softer edges).
  2. **Diff X − Y on binop** — thin bright/dark bands follow the checker edges inside the disk. Outside the disk is nearly perfectly 0 — no information was pushed into the corners, so the diff shows **pure interpolation loss**.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body:
**Takeaway:** every interpolation is a tiny low-pass filter, so more passes with the same total transform means **more high-frequency loss**. In real cryo-EM iterative alignment the standard tactic is **always re-applying the current best (φ, θ, ψ, dx, dy) to the original particle in one pass** — never 'rotate, then rotate again'.

Masking the particle inside a sensible radius before applying rotations/translations is a standard precaution: it avoids the side effect of corner clipping shrinking the effective support each iteration.

**Play with it — watch the error grow with iteration count:**
  • Set DO `end` to **1** → N=1 the diff is 0 (self comparison).
  • `end=6` with Y's `angle_deg=5` → 5° × 6 = 30° total, more cumulative loss.
  • Set Mask's `outer_radius` to **200** so the disk exceeds the box → corner information is now clipped, mixing interpolation loss with mask effects.
  • Set Mask's `edge` to `cosine` → softer rim, less Fourier-ringing (cleaner high-frequency comparison).
  • Drop Rotate (Y)'s `interpolation` from `linear` to `nearest` → more loss per pass → accumulation becomes very obvious.

**Quantify:** wire `stats.moments` to arith.binop's output to read the diff's sigma numerically. Sweep DO `end` 1 → 2 → 3 → … and watch sigma rise monotonically.

**DO + flow.state pattern:** the canonical way to express 'feed this iteration's output into the next'. Alignment iteration, SGD, Newton iteration — any 'apply the same transform until convergence' workflow uses this shape.
